note: The OLG has substantial coverage of SUA policy across multiple pages (Standard Utility Allowance Expense Introduction, HCSUA, Non-Heating SUA, Telephone SUA, Home Energy Assistance Program Payments, Heat and Eat). Key coverage includes: (1) Three SUA types (HCSUA, Non-Heating SUA, Telephone SUA) with only one allowed per household; (2) Massachusetts mandates SUA use — the OLG states 'a standard utility allowance (SUA) is used even when actual expenses exceed the SUA', confirming households cannot use actual expenses; (3) LIHEAP/HEAP entitlement is covered — households receiving HEAP qualify for HCSUA for 12 months, with automated EOHLC data exchange; (4) Heat and Eat (H-EAT) $21 payment program for households that don't pay heating/cooling and don't get HEAP; (5) Public housing with central meters paying excess heating/cooling costs — covered and explicitly eligible for HCSUA; (6) Shared living situations — OLG correctly states each household contributing to utility costs gets the full SUA (no proration), matching the FNS prohibition on prorating. However, several FNS policy details are not explicitly stated in the OLG: (a) the specific eligibility conditions for optional SUA (expense not covered by excluded vendor payment, timing at certification/recertification/move, regular billing requirement) are only partially addressed — the OLG mentions incurring expenses 'separate from rent' but doesn't enumerate the full federal criteria since MA mandates SUA; (b) the OLG does not discuss factors states may use to vary SUAs (household size, region, season) since MA uses uniform statewide amounts; (c) the concept of offering actual expenses as an alternative is absent because MA mandates SUA. These omissions are largely consistent with MA's policy choice to mandate SUA, making the detailed optional-SUA eligibility criteria from FNS less relevant to MA workers.
